issues.description: Problem statement requires Farm to initialize its internal ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments, but the solution's Farm only provides a constructor with an int parameter (Farm(int initialCapacity)) and no zero-argument constructor. This contradicts the explicit requirement and also conflicts with the example usage in Main (new Farm()) present in the template/problem. Students following the instructions or uncommenting the example Main code would encounter a missing no-arg constructor or compilation mismatch.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a no-argument constructor in Farm that initializes animals = new ArrayList<>(), or provide both a no-arg constructor and the existing parameterized constructor. Also ensure example usages (e.g., new Farm()) in Main and the problem statement are consistent with the available constructors.

issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for Farm: the problem statement requires a no-argument constructor that initializes the internal ArrayList, and the template/Main expect Farm() to exist, but the solution implements only Farm(int initialCapacity). This inconsistency prevents students from mapping the described requirement (and the example usage Farm farm = new Farm();) to the provided solution code and would cause compilation confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a public no-argument constructor in Farm that initializes the ArrayList (e.g. public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }) and optionally keep the existing Farm(int initialCapacity) overload. This will align the solution with the problem statement and the template/Main usage.
